events.description: Email Lee at Lsmith@clpvd.org to be added to the email list about upcoming tufting workshops. You will receive a registration link via email when new workshops are scheduled. Learn how to use a tufting machine and create your own rug in this workshop for adults! In this intensive 4-hour workshop for adults, you will learn the basics of using a tufting machine and complete a small rug. The workshop is free, but participants are required to bring their own yarn (two skeins of yarn per color). Yarn should be a medium weight (4) and feed from the center. All participants are required to satisfactorily complete a safety screening checklist and sign a liability waiver before participating. This intensive 4-hour workshop involves using a handheld power tool with sharp, fast-moving scissors and a needle. If you have, or are recovering from, a hand, wrist, arm, shoulder, or joint injury or condition, you should not participate in this program at this time. Additionally, please ask yourself the following safety screening questions before deciding to participate. If the answer to any of these questions is “no,” you should not participate in this program at this time. Can you stand unassisted while holding a 5-pound power tool with both hands for 3 hours? Can you fully understand and follow directions? (This workshop is conducted in English.) Are you complete the project independently? Can you hold the trigger firmly on a vibrating power tool for 3 hours? Do you have the upper body strength to apply pressure with a handheld power tool and maintain your balance in the event of kickback? Can you carefully handle a handheld power tool with a fast-moving needle? Registration through Eventbrite is required. Please register for only one workshop. If you’ve already completed a workshop and wish to continue tufting, you may do so during makerspace open studio hours.

events.summary: This singular new 6-part essay film on the history of the state of Rhode Island, monument (2026), by directors Tim Geraghty and Sarah Halpern , illustrates the adage that the universal is best reached via the particular: the very local…
events.description: This singular new 6-part essay film on the history of the state of Rhode Island, monument (2026), by directors Tim Geraghty and Sarah Halpern , illustrates the adage that the universal is best reached via the particular: the very local issues investigated in the film blossom into a body of insights and speculations extending far beyond the borders of any region. monument weaves statues, plaques, and place names together with the routine movements of everyday life. Readings from history books, monologues from a fictional tour guide, and personal home movies are paired with interviews relating to the Colonial Era, the Slave Trade, the American Revolution, the Industrial Revolution, Indigenous Cultures, the Abolitionist Movement, Organized Crime, Urban Planning, Capitalism, Baseball, Ancient Geology, and Apple Pie. Over time, stories overlap, and voices converge to create a dynamic, multi-layered temporal x-ray, challenging the objectification of history with the animism of storytelling. The screening will be followed by a conversation with the filmmakers, Sarah Halpern and Tim Geraghty. Free. Watch the trailer . Read the review in Screen Slate This program is presented by RISD’s Film, Animation and Video Department and Center for Community Partnerships. Screening and Conversation Schedule 2:00 pm - Screening begins 4:30 pm - Intermission 5:00-7:00 pm - Screening continues 7:00-7:30 pm - Discussion with the filmmakers Tim Geraghty' s experimental films have been called 'radically new' and 'breathtakingly multilayered' by Cineaste Magazine . His feature film The Unicorn (2018) won the International Competition at BAFICI Film Fest (Buenos Aires), the Excellence Award at Indie Memphis and was nominated for Best First Feature at Doc Lisboa. His previous films have screened in venues including the Rotterdam International Film Festival, Anthology Film Archives, B.A.M. events.description: Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series HOW TO WITH JOHN WILSON, NYC documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. events.title: Abigail Rose Clarke presents THE BODY ORACLE DECK, in conversation with Rebecca Atwood and Amy Salamone
events.summary: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478603 --- Brightly soulful and deeply rooted, The Body Oracle Deck is a somatic invitation to awe and wonder, a homecoming to nature and the body, and an antidote…
events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478603 --- Brightly soulful and deeply rooted, The Body Oracle Deck is a somatic invitation to awe and wonder, a homecoming to nature and the body, and an antidote to despair. Includes 80 lushly illustrated cards with original collage art, body-based exercises, and an accompanying guidebook Written by Abigail Rose Clarke (Returning Home to Our Bodies) and illustrated by Amy Salomone, this deck opens our awareness to a profound and powerful truth: our bodies are miracles. Created to help you connect to the innate and beautiful wisdom of your body—and to the living world to which we each belong—The Body Oracle Deck is an invitation into embodied resistance against disembodiment and cynicism. It helps us awaken to ourselves and our senses so we can awaken to the world—and stay present and engaged even through heartbreak and hopelessness. Structured in four sections, Clarke guides us through four dimensions of embodied knowing: * “Awe”: tiny stories of our beginnings—as stardust, as kin—that open us to a greater sense of wonder * “Curiosity”: meditations on safety, change, intuition, and belief—that are meant to change and evolve as you do * “Possibilities”: breath, movement, and imaginative engagement with your body * “Oracle”: the body’s wisdom on vitality, reciprocity, and integration Muscle and blood, belly and bone, our bodies move and connect more like ecosystems than machines. This deck offers a path home to this truth—and a conduit to the precious, singular experiences and sensations that make up what it means to be vital, embodied, and fully alive.

On the Brooklyn waterfront, longshoreman Eddie Carbone lives by a strict code of loyalty, family, and respect. But when two undocumented cousins arrive from Sicily seeking work, Eddie’s tightly controlled world begins to unravel. His growing obsession with his niece Catherine sets off a chain reaction of suspicion, betrayal, and devastating consequences. In one of the most powerful tragedies of the American stage, Miller lays bare the destructive force of jealousy and pride.

events.title: Lez Zeppelin
events.summary: The all-female quartet, personally endorsed by Jimmy Page.
events.description: In honor of the 50th anniversary of the release of The Song Remains the Same, internationally acclaimed Lez Zeppelin — the all-female quartet known for delivering the most powerful and authentic Led Zeppelin experience and the only band personally endorsed by Jimmy Page, himself, announces a special concert series celebrating the iconic 1976 film and its legendary soundtrack. Accompanied by a multimedia presentation inspired by the original movie, Lez Zeppelin will perform the soundtrack from The Song Remains the Same in its entirety. Harnessing the energy, virtuosity, and grandeur of Led Zeppelin’s storied 1973 performances at Madison Square Garden, this tribute is more than a concert — it’s a resurrection of rock history, reimagined and re-ignited for a new generation. "This film and soundtrack are sacred ground for Zeppelin fans and musicians alike," says Steph Paynes, founder and guitarist of Lez Zeppelin. "To play it from top to bottom — complete with the cinematic scope and improvisational fire of the original — is a challenge we embrace with deep reverence and fierce joy." The tour will feature jaw-dropping renditions of classics like “No Quarter,” “Dazed and Confused,” “Since I’ve Been Loving You,” and the transcendent “Stairway to Heaven.” Each show will be an immersive and unique experience designed to channel the mystique and raw power that made The Song Remains the Same a cornerstone of rock cinema. Whether you grew up with the film or are discovering it for the first time, this series promises to honor Zeppelin’s legacy with the stunning authenticity and fearless performances for which Lez Zeppelin are known and celebrated worldwide.

events.title: Jim Shepard reading from THE QUEEN OF BAD INFLUENCES, in conversation with Gary Zebrun
events.summary: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478604 --- Twelve compressed masterworks from this great American writer of catastrophe fiction, in which lives are upended as much by broken hearts as by collapsing…
events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478604 --- Twelve compressed masterworks from this great American writer of catastrophe fiction, in which lives are upended as much by broken hearts as by collapsing dams, hideously mismanaged wars, gargantuan wildfires, and apocalyptic storms “Jim Shepard is a fantastic writer—compassionate, funny, and fearless—[whose work] does what great writing always does: inspires us to look more closely at life, and be more caring.” —George Saunders “A deft, audacious artist.” —Norman Rush, National Book Award-winning author of Mating In Richard Ford’s view, Jim Shepard’s “talent is so various and canny he can write about seemingly anything and make it thrilling to us,” and in these stories spanning six centuries we find viscerally evoked worlds as wildly diverse as a mercenary’s corner of 16th century Madrid, a young apprentice’s pre-Revolutionary Boston, and Edward Hyde’s London. With civil engineers and destitute veterans we encounter the devastating 1935 Labor Day hurricane in Florida, and we read the 1864 letters between Lucy in Boon, North Carolina (“Three privates are currently sleeping soundly on our porch in their muddy blankets”) and her great love, William, on the march in Tennessee (“I can’t write much for it seems we are looking for a fight every minute”), while the title story introduces us to the stubborn Constance, who had “no gift for flirtation” with men, preferring Minna, her best friend and “queen of bad influences,” as their vexed devotion unfolds in part on the liner Lusitania. With irony, compassion, and withering humor, these stories evoke the terrible ease with which cataclysm, human-engineered or otherwise, can sweep away all we find most precious, and expose those limitations we’ve refused to address. At the same time, Shepard celebrates what is best in us: the love and friendships we sustain, and the passions and grace we grant one another.

tags: museum of natural history and planetarium
events.summary: You will have the opportunity to discover, or rediscover, the fascinating collections during this private program exploring the Museum of Natural History and Planetarium in Roger Williams Park.
events.description: You will have the opportunity to discover, or rediscover, the fascinating collections during this private program exploring the Museum of Natural History and Planetarium in Roger Williams Park. Bring a small easel or chair and your drawing or painting materials, and choose your subject from the collections of birds, bears, lions, and Oceanic artifacts. Museum staff will also select some special “guests” from the museum vaults to display. During the program, the instructor will circulate for those who wish feedback, and at the end of the session, attendees will gather to view and discuss each other’s work. Please note: Museum is closed to the public during this program. Program fee: $35 per adult/ $30 for museum members . Pre-registration required. Permitted Materials: You may bring the medium of your choice — charcoal pencils, graphite, colored pencils, pastels, or watercolor (please, no oils or acrylics). All skill levels are welcome to participate, high school age and older. Capacity is limited, so sign up early to guarantee your spot. INSTRUCTOR: KATHY HODGE : Kathy Hodge attended RISD and has a BFA in painting from Swain School of Design. She has been working in oils and charcoal for over 30 years, has exhibited widely and was awarded the 2017 Fellowship in Painting from the Rhode Island State Council on the Arts. Kathy has long taken inspiration from the natural world in her landscape paintings and was appointed Artist in Residence in thirteen of our National Parks and Forests. She first discovered the museum collections when taking a museum class and she is very excited to be able to offer this opportunity to draw from the collections.

events.title: Nathanael Greene, Rhode Island, and the Race to the Dan with Andrew Waters
events.summary: Join the Rhode Island Historical Society on Monday, November 9th at 6pm for the presentation Nathanael Greene, Rhode Island, and the Race to the Dan by author Andrew Waters.
events.description: Join the Rhode Island Historical Society on Monday, November 9th at 6pm for the presentation Nathanael Greene, Rhode Island, and the Race to the Dan by author Andrew Waters. In this program, Waters explores how Nathanael Greene’s Rhode Island upbringing shaped his military leadership during the Revolutionary War, focusing on the Race to the Dan—Greene’s strategic retreat across North and South Carolina. As commander of the Continental Army’s overmatched Southern Department, Greene relied on adaptation, resilience, and critical thinking to outmaneuver Charles Cornwallis and help prevent the British from regaining control of the South. Through pivotal moments in the Race to the Dan, Waters examines how Greene’s early life and experiences in Rhode Island influenced the leadership qualities that made his campaign so consequential. Andrew Waters is the author of three books on the American Revolution in the South, including To the End of the World: Nathanael Greene, Charles Cornwallis, and the Race to the Dan. His most recent book, Backcountry War: The Rise Francis Marion, Banastre Tarleton, and Thomas Sumter was a finalist for the American Battlefield Trust’s “Book Prize for History.” After an early career in editing and publishing, he has spent the majority of his career working in land conservation. Andrew is a North Carolina native, where he currently resides with his wife, Anne, and cat, Romeo. Register now here .

events.title: Dave Matthews Band
events.summary: Dave Matthews Band was the highest-ranked American headliner on Pollstar’s list of the “25 Most Popular Touring Artists of The Millenium,” coming in at No. 4.
events.description: Dave Matthews Band was the highest-ranked American headliner on Pollstar’s list of the “25 Most Popular Touring Artists of The Millenium,” coming in at No. 4. Since debuting in 1991, Dave Matthews Band has sold more than 25 million tickets, making them the second-largest ticket seller in history, and a combined 38 million CDs and DVDs. Named as a UN Environment Goodwill Ambassador in 2019, Dave Matthews Band has a long history of reducing its environmental footprint, going back to its first shows in 1991. This fall, the band will continue its partnership with Live Nation venues to further minimize the environmental footprint of its tour. 2026 marks the third year of the “On The Road To Zero Waste Tour,” which achieved a milestone of over 90% of fan-generated waste at Live Nation venues composted recycled or donated in previous years. Dave Matthews Band will once again join forces with environmental nonprofit REVERB, celebrating 21 years of partnership focused on making the music industry more sustainable and fan-driven action more measurable. In 2026, Dave Matthews Band continues its long‑standing support of The Nature Conservancy’s global reforestation efforts. Seven years strong, this work is rooted in a simple belief that healthy forests help create a healthier planet. With this year’s tour, the band will have planted a total of 7 million trees by the end of 2026. These trees help rebuild critical forests that clean our air and water, provide habitat for wildlife, and support a more stable climate for future generations. Learn more about this work with The Nature Conservancy at dmbtrees.org.

events.summary: You’ve got your research question—now, how do you actually find the sources you need? With hundreds of databases available, where should you start, and how do you know if you’re searching effectively?
events.description: You’ve got your research question—now, how do you actually find the sources you need? With hundreds of databases available, where should you start, and how do you know if you’re searching effectively? Join librarians as we tackle these challenges in our Find Research Materials Workshop. We’ll demystify the database landscape, distinguishing between broad discovery tools like BruKnow and discipline-specific databases tailored to your field. You’ll practice translating your own keywords into the controlled vocabulary that databases use, and learn to identify “seed articles” that can anchor and expand your research. This workshop is designed to help undergraduate researchers develop strategic, efficient search skills and is part of a four-part series for students in the early stages of thesis work or those looking to strengthen their approach before the next phase of their project. Event registration is preferred. Please contact micah_saxton@brown.edu with any questions.

events.title: RISD Photo Gary Metz Lecture - Birthe Piontek
events.summary: Birthe Piontek is a visual artist who works in photography, installation, sculpture, and drawing. Her photographic practice explores the interconnections between photographic images, objects, history, and personal and collective memory.
events.description: Birthe Piontek is a visual artist who works in photography, installation, sculpture, and drawing. Her photographic practice explores the interconnections between photographic images, objects, history, and personal and collective memory. Piontek’s work has been exhibited in solo and group shows in Canada, the United States, Europe, and South America and is featured in many private and public collections, such as the Museum of Contemporary Photography in Chicago and the Museum of Applied Arts in Gera, Germany. Piontek is the author of several photography books. The project The Idea of North won the Critical Mass Book Award in 2009 and was published by Photolucida in 2011. Her project Abendlied received the Edward Burtynsky Grant in 2018 and was nominated by Time Magazine as one of the best photo books in 2019. Her third book, Janus , was published in 2021, and her newest project, Zero Hour , was released in 2025. Piontek received her MFA from the Folkwang University of the Arts in Essen, Germany. She lives in Vancouver, Canada, where she is an Associate Professor of Photography at the Emily Carr University of Art and Design. On the Brooklyn waterfront, longshoreman Eddie Carbone lives by a strict code of loyalty, family, and respect. But when two undocumented cousins arrive from Sicily seeking work, Eddie’s tightly controlled world begins to unravel. His growing obsession with his niece Catherine sets off a chain reaction of suspicion, betrayal, and devastating consequences. events.description: Syrian-American comedian Nasser Al-Rayess, popularly known as @naw_sir and the “Shawarma King,” has rapidly risen as a dynamic force in the comedy world. Through his sharp wit and exploration of his Arab-American identity, Nasser offers a refreshing take on pop culture and current events. His keen observational humor, especially around identity and popular Arab music, has garnered him over a million followers across social media. Nasser’s impact reaches far beyond the digital realm as he has toured across the country with his stand-up comedy, gracing stages in New York City, Los Angeles, Dubai, and more. His stand-up comedy showcases his innovative comedy style, blending humor, Arabic music, and the warm ambiance of a traditional Arab gathering, leaving audiences of all backgrounds entertained and embraced. Aspiring to revolutionize Arab-American comedy, Nasser is pushing Arab culture into the mainstream. His journey of unapologetic self-acceptance continues to captivate audiences, as he leads the way in representing and celebrating Arab-American and Arab diaspora voices in comedy. events.summary: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478622 --- A groundbreaking hybrid memoir, She Was Wild Grass deftly intertwines Bennett’s own artistic coming-of-age with the haunting story of Joan Vollmer, the…
events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478622 --- A groundbreaking hybrid memoir, She Was Wild Grass deftly intertwines Bennett’s own artistic coming-of-age with the haunting story of Joan Vollmer, the remarkable yet overlooked figure of the Beat Generation whose life was tragically cut short when her husband, William S. Burroughs, shot her in 1951. Braiding past and present, Bennett explores art, ambition, gender, and freedom, asking what it means to create in a world where women’s stories are so often silenced and forgotten. At once intimate and unflinching, it brings Vollmer out from the shadows of literary history while charting the risks and revelations of Bennett’s own search for an artistic path. For readers of Kate Zambreno, Maggie Nelson, and Nathalie Léger, She Was Wild Grass offers an unflinching meditation on art, history, and self-discovery.

This approach allows fans both young and old to share in the experience while offering a continually evolving artistic outlet within this musical canon.DARK STAR ORCHESTRA offers much more than just the sound of the Grateful Dead—they truly encapsulate the energy and experience. It’s about that sense of familiarity and contagious energy that creates the complete concert experience fans expect.The band has featured guest performances from six original Grateful Dead members: Phil Lesh, Bob Weir, Bill Kreutzmann, Donna Jean Godchaux-MacKay, Vince Welnick, and Tom Constanten, plus longtime Dead soundman Dan Healy. Other notable guests have included Mike Gordon and Jon Fishman of Phish, Warren Haynes, Steve Kimock, and many more.“For us it’s a chance to recreate some of the magic that was created for us over the years,” explains keyboardist and vocalist Rob Barraco. “We offer a sort of historical perspective at what it might have been like to go to a show in 1985, 1978 or whenever. Even for Deadheads who can say they’ve been to a hundred shows in the 90s, we offer something they never got to see live.”

Step back in time to explore the Betsey Williams Cottage, built in 1773 and home to Roger Williams’ great-great-great granddaughters, Betsey and Rhoda Williams. Upon her death in 1871, Betsey Williams bequeathed the cottage and 102 acres of surrounding farmland to the city of Providence, which became the foundation of Roger Williams Park. Drop-in during these FREE open houses to learn about the Cottage’s history and its significance to Roger Williams Park. The open houses are FREE and open to the public. events.summary: Amelia Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, days away from completing her record-setting flight around the world. The official search was abandoned after 16 days. The unofficial search has never ended.
events.description: Amelia Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, days away from completing her record-setting flight around the world. The official search was abandoned after 16 days. The unofficial search has never ended. In Lost: Amelia Earhart’s Three Mysterious Deaths and One Extraordinary Life , Rachel Hartigan retraces the three main theories of Earhart’s disappearance, introducing a cast of eccentric characters consumed by discovering the truth. Did the aviator and her navigator fly off course to spy on Japanese military bases, only to be captured? Did they land on a remote Pacific island—where Hartigan traveled—and die as castaways? Or did they run out of fuel and crash into the ocean? Hartigan, a former National Geographic writer, intersperses the search for Earhart with the story of Earhart’s extraordinary life—her unstable childhood, her itinerant early career, and her unconventional marriage to a PR-savvy publisher who transformed her into an aviation icon—and illuminates why we remember Amelia Earhart today.

events.title: Lucy Darling: The More the Merrier
events.summary: With more than 4 million followers across social media, what began as a beloved stage character has become one of live entertainment’s fastest-growing success stories.
events.description: With more than 4 million followers across social media, what began as a beloved stage character has become one of live entertainment’s fastest-growing success stories. A clip from one of Lucy Darling’s live performances went viral in late 2024, and since then, more than 150,000 people have attended her shows. Fans now travel across North America to see Lucy, often returning multiple times and bringing friends and family into the devoted Darling community. It’s a testament to the character’s signature blend of world-class magic, glamour, and spontaneity. In The More the Merrier , Lucy continues her vivacious vagabond voyages with a touring variety show featuring her unquestionable advice and, for the first time, two delightful companions. Pianist TJ Shanoff provides a fully improvised musical soundtrack to Lucy's running commentary, while multi-instrumentalist Mark Ettinger brings an ever-changing collection of instruments — and a few surprises of his own — to the stage. Together, the trio delivers an evening of comedy, music, magic, and audience interaction where every performance is different and no two nights are ever the same. Whether you’re meeting Lucy Darling for the first time or have been part of the journey for years, The More The Merrier offers an evening that’s equal parts heartfelt, hilarious, and completely unforgettable.

events.summary: PUNCH BROTHERS , formed by mandolinist Chris Thile in 2006, is known for pushing the boundaries of acoustic music. In addition to Thile, the band currently comprises guitarist Chris Eldridge, bassist Paul Kowert, banjoist Noam Pikelny, and…
events.description: PUNCH BROTHERS , formed by mandolinist Chris Thile in 2006, is known for pushing the boundaries of acoustic music. In addition to Thile, the band currently comprises guitarist Chris Eldridge, bassist Paul Kowert, banjoist Noam Pikelny, and violinist Brittany Haas. Punch Brothers has garnered critical acclaim, including a Grammy for Best Folk Album for All Ashore (2018). The Washington Post applauded them for taking “bluegrass to its next evolutionary stage, drawing equal inspiration from the brain and the heart.” Over the past two decades, Punch Brothers has become a pioneer in modern string music, with albums like Antifogmatic (2010), Who’s Feeling Young Now (2012), and The Phosphorescent Blues (2015) showcasing the group’s genre-defying sound. Rolling Stone praised their work as “wild virtuosity used for more than just virtuosity,” cementing their reputation as trailblazers in contemporary acoustic music. The band’s most recent album, Hell on Church Street (2021), is a reimagining of, and homage to, the late bluegrass great Tony Rice’s landmark solo album Church Street Blues . Most recently, Punch Brothers have been focused on the band’s musical variety show, The Energy Curfew Music Hour. Season One is available on all podcast platforms, with season two exclusively out on Audible. Season 1 was nominated for a Webby Award in the Podcast: Features, Experimental & Innovation category; it also won Most Innovative Audio Experience, Best Live Podcast Recording, and Best Sound Design in the Listener’s Choice category of the 2025 Signal Awards. The Unsung Adventures of Punch Brothers , the seventh album from the Grammy-winning band—and its first comprising all instrumental tunes as well as its first with fiddle player Brittany Haas, who joined the quintet in 2023—is due July 24, 2026, on Nonesuch Records. The album features eight new original compositions by Punch Brothers as well as three traditional songs they arranged.

events.summary: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478623 --- A revolutionary way of seeing bodies and built environment that unites radical politics and trans aesthetics.
events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/478623 --- A revolutionary way of seeing bodies and built environment that unites radical politics and trans aesthetics. From a leading author and queer theorist known for reframing many of the most pressing questions about counter-intuitive ways of being. Anarchitecture, a radical aesthetic practice of unmaking the built environment, staged a vigorous confrontation with urban renewal and gentrification projects in the 1970s. In Anarchitecture After Everything, Jack Halberstam identifies a powerful lexicon of transformation within anarchitecture, joining the movement’s practices of cutting and splitting with the destabilizing power of transness to detonate acts of formal violence in our time. Anarchitecture describes the aesthetic practice of splitting and cutting, dismantling and undoing, unmaking, unbuilding, and ultimately unworlding. The trans body splits bodily coherence, dismantles the gender binary, and unbuilds bodily meaning. In these chapters, Gordon Matta-Clark’s cuts, along with Alvin Baltrop’s 1970s images of collapsing warehouses and Beverly Buchanan’s post-demolition fragmentary sculptures, return with a vengeance through the contemporary aesthetic gestures of Yve Laris Cohen, Jesse Darling, Nicole Eisenman, Kiyan Williams, Cassils, boychild, and Every Ocean Hughes. Anarchitecture unmakes space and offers a new rhetoric for emptiness. In its conclusion, the book explores this rhetoric through Renee Gladman’s anarchitectural experiments with language. By reading anarchitecture through transness and transness through anarchitecture, Halberstam helps us see the trans body as a space of radical unmaking and as a portal to new lexicons for transformation.

events.summary: From the team that brought you Come See Me in the Good Light, join us for Andrea Gibson’s Love Letter from the Afterlife— a multimedia event bringing together film, live poetry, music, orchestral accompaniment, and intimate storytelling in…
events.description: From the team that brought you Come See Me in the Good Light, join us for Andrea Gibson’s Love Letter from the Afterlife— a multimedia event bringing together film, live poetry, music, orchestral accompaniment, and intimate storytelling in a celebration of one of the most beloved voices of a generation. At the heart of each evening is Love Letter from the Afterlife , a stunning film capturing Andrea Gibson’s final live performance: a brilliant, brave, tender, and raucous poetry set recorded at Denver’s Paramount Theatre in 2024. The film was produced by the team behind the Oscar-nominated documentary, Come See Me in the Good Light. Throughout the event, The Goosebumps Orchestra will perform Blake Neely’s original score live alongside Gibson’s filmed performance, creating a deeply immersive experience that expands the poetry beyond the screen. Guest artists will join throughout the night, coupled with film and performances that will transform each stop into a living, breathing composition and a singular celebration of Gibson’s work. Created between New York and Los Angeles, the project explores themes of love, identity, and emotional transformation — capturing a period of both personal and artistic evolution.

Do you admire legendary artists such as Smokey Robinson, Marvin Gaye, The Temptations, The Supremes, and The Four Tops? If so, you're in for a treat! That Motown Band brings together a remarkable ensemble of talented vocalists and musicians dedicated to keeping the Motown spirit alive. For years, they’ve been captivating audiences with their incredible performances and timeless music. Come and experience the timeless magic of Motown music like never before! Joining the Motown Band is Garfield Fleming. Garfield is a Soul Singing Vocalist of legendary status having been a member of The Delfonics for 25 years with William Hart. Garfield’s obvious resemblance to David Ruffin makes people look twice but when he sings fans get lost in time! He sounds just like Bobby Womack, David Ruffin and can also perform the songs of many legendary artists. In 1981 Garfield released a single “Please Don’t Send Me Away” which is still played all over the world. He gained much of his fame as a solo artist with that song and was received very well in many countries all over the world. The musical director for That Motown Band is Tom Schizzano. Tom is a multi-instrumentalist, arranger, and vocalist. He has written and produced music for worldwide release on television shows and advertising. His credits include CBS/Paramount, Disney, PBS and NBC/Universal. He has performed live with artists such as Hall & Oates, Cindy Lauper, Lou Christie and Paul Shaffer. He has also produced and arranged music for recording artists in the pop and oldies genre such as The Tokens and Jimmy Clanton. Tom has scored several independent films and continues to write, arrange, and produce from his production studio in Hauppauge New York. This is a 4PM matinee show.

events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/479705 --- sipèstisyon unflinchingly navigates generational trauma, migration, and spirituality. In this powerful debut, Haitian-American poet Mckendy Fils-Aimé examines wounds left by abuse, familial estrangement, and racial violence. Through the lens of Haitian superstitions, sipèstisyon explores the imperfect and non-linear nature of healing. These poems don’t pretend that moving on is as simple as moving on. They know that mending a wound requires understanding its shape and origin and that confrontation is sometimes necessary. In each poem, sipèstisyon asks which is louder: the sound of our ache or the call to forgive?

events.title: 205th Annual Meeting of the Rhode Island Historical Society
events.summary: Rhode Island Historical Society members are invited on Monday, November 16, at 5:30 PM to our 205th Annual Meeting, where RIHS members will gather to hear from the Board of Trustees and Executive Leadership about the organization’s…
events.description: Rhode Island Historical Society members are invited on Monday, November 16, at 5:30 PM to our 205th Annual Meeting, where RIHS members will gather to hear from the Board of Trustees and Executive Leadership about the organization’s accomplishments over the past year, including our commemorations of the nation’s 250th anniversary. Following meeting business, we will welcome distinguished scholar and Ambassador-at-Large at the Smithsonian Institution Richard Kurin as this year’s featured speaker. Kurin will discuss his new book, History by a Hair , which explores the remarkable story of a strand of hair found in Thomas Jefferson’s Bible and the decades-long effort to use DNA technology to help resolve a 200-year-old historical mystery. The work has been covered widely, including by The New Yorker, NPR, The Today Show, and The New York Times. We are thrilled to offer our members the opportunity to hear more about the project and its findings. The meeting will also include a dinner buffet and book signing. RIHS members can register by visiting the membership portal . Should you have any questions about the meeting please contact membership@rihs.org .

events.summary: When it comes to censorship, few examples come close to the backlash Salman Rushdie faced for The Satanic verses . Though awarded many times over for his various works, regularly short-listed for a nobel prize in literature, and even…
events.description: When it comes to censorship, few examples come close to the backlash Salman Rushdie faced for The Satanic verses . Though awarded many times over for his various works, regularly short-listed for a nobel prize in literature, and even knighted in 2007, Salman Rushdie has spent the better part of 40 years living in safe houses due to active threats on his life, but what is this controversial work of early magical realism even about? Let’s find out together. For more information email jleibrandt@clpvd.org.

events.description: 1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (VANYA) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success. events.title: Research Fundamentals: Evaluate Research Materials
events.summary: You’ve found sources—but how do you know which ones are worth your time? This workshop teaches you to evaluate scholarly materials efficiently and critically before committing to a full read.
events.description: You’ve found sources—but how do you know which ones are worth your time? This workshop teaches you to evaluate scholarly materials efficiently and critically before committing to a full read. You’ll learn to mine library records for key decision-making information like abstracts, subject terms, and citation data. We’ll break down the anatomy of scholarly articles so you can navigate them strategically rather than reading every word. Finally, you’ll practice a three-step reading approach—triage, skim, and deep read—that helps you manage dozens of sources without sacrificing critical engagement. Event registration is preferred. Please contact micah_saxton@brown.edu with any questions.

events.title: “Northern Comfort” book signing in partnership with Charter Books at the Colony House Holiday Market Sip & Shop
events.summary: Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 4pm to 7pm | Book Signing Event* The Colony House | Washington Square, Newport *This event takes place during the Opening Celebration of the Holiday Market at the Colony House Sip & Shop Hosted in partnership…
events.description: Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 4pm to 7pm | Book Signing Event* The Colony House | Washington Square, Newport *This event takes place during the Opening Celebration of the Holiday Market at the Colony House Sip & Shop Hosted in partnership with Charter Books, the NHS is proud to present authors Kathleen Fitzgerald & Keith Stavely for a book signing event for their cookbook, Northern Comfort: The New England Baking Tradition. In the wake of the American Revolution, a culinary style formed that would set the standard for American cooking. In Northern Comfort, acclaimed food historians Keith Stavely and Kathleen Fitzgerald draw history lovers and home cooks alike into the kitchen with fifty-two recipes for breads, pies, cookies, and cakes. Readers will bake alongside the abolitionist kneading dough for her immensely popular white bread, the teacher frosting one of the world’s first layer cakes, and the housewife cutting through the thick crust of a meat pie. The result is a delicious, intimate journey through the lives of everyday people who built our nation. From comparing the meals of patriots and loyalists to mediating long-running disputes over the best way to make Johnny cakes, Northern Comfort offers a taste of life in historic New England that is as enticing as the baked goods themselves. RSVPs are recommended but not required. RSVP by clicking the “RSVP Here” button below. RSVP Here! Please Note: Because this event takes place as the same evening as the Opening Night Sip & Shop at the Colony House Holiday market, the registration page will be the same.

events.description: Self-help Singh is the alter ego of international comedian Masood Boomgaard. Self-help Singh, described as a comedic alternative life coach and de-motivational speaker, first appeared to Boomgaard in a vision after he fell and hit his head while rushing to the bathroom in an attempt to outrun the gastric consequences of bad lamb vindaloo. Boomgaard has since been sharing the "common sense wisdom" and de-motivational teachings of Self-help Singh to millions of people on the internet. The Self-help Singh live show is a hilarious yet thought provoking juxtaposition of stand-up comedy, parody and motivational speaking. During his decade long full time professional comedy career Boomgaard has performed in New York, London, Dubai and during the lockdown, in his father's garage. He lives in South Africa with his cat...for now. Tickets: https://www.ricomedyconnection.com/events/masood-boomgaard-2026

events.description: Do you have your own creative project in mind? We have makerspace equipment, tools, and supplies that might be useful! Some smaller hand tools and art supplies that are available include: a button/pin maker, tracing light pad, cutting mat with rotary cutters, iron, clamps, painting supplies, stencil brushes, Perler beads, hot glue, ribbon, yarn, corner rounder punch, and more. Feel free to stop by to use one of these tools during an open studio session! In addition, we offer access to machines including: Silhouette and Cricut cutting machines, sewing machines, a sublimation printer, a 3D printer, an Epilog laser cutter, and heat presses for fabric and mugs. If you are new to using one of these machines, it is best to receive an introductory lesson by appointment first to learn the basics. To begin using one of the machines, please follow these steps: First, we encourage you to request a training to learn the basics of a specific machine beforehand. We can set up a separate appointment to meet with you during the week. After you are trained, continue working on independent projects during open studio sessions! This month, we are hosting studio sessions for adults on Monday evenings 5:00-7:30, Wednesday mornings 10:00-1:00, and Friday afternoons 1:00-5:00 at Rochambeau Library. If you are planning to attend a particular studio session, it is helpful to RSVP with Garrett at glocke@clpvd.org so we can predict which machines will be in demand.

events.summary: “Family business” refers both to the domestic scale fala nearly always addresses and to the fragile scale of the practice itself.
events.description: “Family business” refers both to the domestic scale fala nearly always addresses and to the fragile scale of the practice itself. Through a selection of recent projects, many still unpublished, the lecture explores houses and collective housing as a continuous field of investigation: familiar programmes producing unfamiliar spaces, where everyday routines meet unlikely geometries, material contrasts, and deliberate contradictions. Filipe Magalhães is an architect and co-founder of fala, based in Porto, Portugal and Lausanne, Switzerland. He graduated from the University of Porto, where he also completed his PhD, and worked with Harry Gugger in Basel and Sanaa in Tokyo. Alongside his practice, he teaches at the Yale School of Architecture and is Chief Curator of Architecture at MAC/CCB in Lisbon.

events.title: Japanese Chigiri-e Workshop: Autumn-Themed Card Making
events.summary: Discover the meditative and tactile beauty of Chigiri-e, a traditional Japanese art form using hand-torn Washi paper to create painterly images.
events.description: Discover the meditative and tactile beauty of Chigiri-e, a traditional Japanese art form using hand-torn Washi paper to create painterly images. In this 2-hour workshop, you will learn foundational techniques for softening and shaping paper edges to build texture and depth, achieving a vibrant, layered effect through paper alone. We will focus on process over perfection in a screen-free, mindful environment designed to foster relaxation and creative focus. Participants will explore a variety of paper textures from plant-based Washi papers to tree-pulp based accent papers. By the end of the session, you will take home a handcrafted collage card and the skills to continue practicing this sustainable art form. About the Instructor Chihiro is a mixed-media artist based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, specializing in traditional Japanese paper arts. Her primary focus is Chigiri-e (hand-torn paper collage), alongside Origami (paper folding), Kiri-e (paper cutting), and Hariko (paper-mâché). As the founder of 5U3 Workshop ( www.5U3.jp ), her work centers on creating screen-free, tactile spaces where anyone can find a sense of calm, belonging, and the simple joy of creating by hand. This event is by registration only. To register, please email cgomes@clpvd.org.

America’s First Adventure to China: A Book & Exhibit Talk with Dr. John R. Haddad
events.venue: The Museum at the John Brown House
events.summary: In 1784, freshly independent American merchants set sail for China with bold ambitions: to strike it rich, convert a civilization, and even command armies.
events.description: In 1784, freshly independent American merchants set sail for China with bold ambitions: to strike it rich, convert a civilization, and even command armies. There was only one problem—the Chinese authorities had no idea the United States existed. How did a nation of novice traders with no knowledge of Chinese customs, language, or complex trade rules go from complete outsiders after the Revolutionary War to challenging global superpowers in just a few short decades? On Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:30 pm the Museum at the John Brown House will explore this topic with historian and author Dr. John R. Haddad as he unpacks the high-stakes, colorful, and often controversial origins of U.S.-China relations. Drawing from his acclaimed book, America’s First Adventure to China, and the Museum at the John Brown House’s new exhibit that the book is based upon, Rhode Island’s First Adventure to China, 1787-1815, Dr. Haddad will reveal how an improvisational spirit, high-stakes opium smuggling, and missionary zeal shaped America’s presence in Asia—and how it played a pivotal role in the economic development of early America and Rhode Island. Dr. John R. Haddad is Interim Director of the School of Humanities and Professor of American Studies and Popular Culture at Penn State Harrisburg. A former Fulbright Scholar at the University of Hong Kong, he holds degrees from Harvard, Yale, and University of Texas Austin. He is the author of three books exploring America’s historical relationship with China, including America’s First Adventure in China: Trade, Treaties, Opium, and Salvation, which directly inspired this exhibit. Doors open at 4:30 pm for a book signing, reception, and the chance to explore the exhibit; the talk starts promptly at 5:30 pm. Seating is limited; advance registration is highly encouraged. In the story a man is drawn into a celestial paradise painted on a wall. What first unfolds as a realm of desire slowly darkens into fear, as an armored official appears in search of an intruder. The painted world shifts with the movements of the mind, where desire and dread give shape to what seems real. Self-Haunted revisits the painted wall as both an image and a boundary, inviting entry while holding the power to expel. Across the exhibition, images beckon, linger, and quietly return our gaze. As enchantment gives way to scrutiny, the worlds we conjure begin to haunt us, shaping how we see and are seen.

On the Brooklyn waterfront, longshoreman Eddie Carbone lives by a strict code of loyalty, family, and respect. But when two undocumented cousins arrive from Sicily seeking work, Eddie’s tightly controlled world begins to unravel. In one of the most powerful tragedies of the American stage, Miller lays bare the destructive force of jealousy and pride.

events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/479708 --- LONGLISTED FOR THE CENTER FOR FICTION FIRST NOVEL PRIZE An ensemble cast collides and crosses paths in their small corner of the Midwest where no one is a stranger: the baker, the realtor, the poet, the gardener, the frustrated artist. In Devon Halliday’s transcendent debut novel, secrets turn contagious, impulses transform into resolutions, and no one is certain whether they will remain in the confines of their Appalachian college town or step out into the unknown. Surrounded by hills, buried in green, Eden is a forgotten town full of ordinary lives. But over the course of a humid summer week, seven of these ordinary lives reach their boiling point, as the existential questions of each begin to urgently entwine. Underneath the threat of marital infidelity, financial ruin, and life-changing illness is always the same question: To stay, or to go? If you choose to stay, is it ever a permanent choice? Can you be sure you’ll choose it again tomorrow? A mosaic portrait of love and its close substitutes, the novel suggests, fearfully, that even our best decisions might be fragile, arbitrary, and impermanent.

To their inland West was the Ashokan reservoir folk tradition, and across the river to the East the legacy of Pete Seeger and the Clearwater. Marky Ramone is best known for the 15 years he spent drumming for the legendary Ramones. Prior to joining the Ramones, Marky played with an array of influential musicians dating back to his high school years when he was a member of the Brooklyn based hard rock band, Dust. Recording two albums with his friends, Richie Wise (guitar and vocals) and Kenny Aaronson (bass) for Neil Bogart’s Karma Sutra/Buddha label. While Dust was disbanding, Marky began hanging out at Max’s Kansas City, where he met Max’s house D.J. Wayne County. He joined forces with Wayne to form Wayne County and The Backstreet Boys. Wayne’s outrageous stage performance and cross-dressing attracted many fans and help solidify a cult following. After a year and a half of playing in the New York area and not able to generate record company interest, they decided it was best to move on. In 1976, Marky was introduced to Richard Hell. Along with Bob Quine and Ivan Julian, they formed Richard Hell & the Voidoids. The Voidoids released their groundbreaking debut album in 1977 on Sire Records, entitled “Blank Generation”. Shortly after the Voidoids historic U.K. tour with The Clash, Marky found himself at the bar at CBGB with Dee Dee Ramone. Dee Dee asked him if he would be interested in joining The Ramones. The spring of 1978, Marky joined the Ramones. events.description: Free Open Houses at the Betsey Williams Cottage in Roger Williams Park on Fridays, 10am-3pm! Step back in time to explore the Betsey Williams Cottage, built in 1773 and home to Roger Williams’ great-great-great granddaughters, Betsey and Rhoda Williams. Upon her death in 1871, Betsey Williams bequeathed the cottage and 102 acres of surrounding farmland to the city of Providence, which became the foundation of Roger Williams Park. Drop-in during these FREE open houses to learn about the Cottage’s history and its significance to Roger Williams Park. The open houses are FREE and open to the public. Presented by the Museum of Natural History and Planetarium . The Betsey Williams Cottage is located near Roger Williams Park’s Elmwood Avenue entrance. Parking is available on streets surrounding the Rose Garden; see a Roger Williams Park map .

events.description: Actor/Comedian/Writer Nick Thune’s deadpan delivery and absurdist storytelling has made him a standout in the comedy world. Originally from Seattle, Thune built his name on late-night stages, racking up ten appearances on The Tonight Show, along with spots on Conan and Late Night. He went on to tour internationally and headline major comedy festivals including Montreal’s Just for Laughs, SXSW, Bonnaroo, and Melbourne International. Thune has released three stand-up specials: Folk Hero (Netflix) and Good Guy (Amazon), and Born Young, which premiered on Nate Bargatze’s Nateland YouTube channel. His material blends sharp one-liners with personal storytelling with guitar, making him a favorite among longtime comedy fans and new audiences alike. On screen, he’s appeared in Judd Apatow’s Knocked Up, Marvel’s Venom, and cult indie Dave Made a Maze, with TV credits including HBO Max’s Love Life, Hulu’s How I Met Your Father, ABC’s Not Dead Yet, Grand Crew and voice work on American Dad!. In 2025, Nick’s short film “BDAY Private Dick” with John C. Reilly premiered at the Palm Springs Film Festival. Currently, Thune is developing a podcast with Mary Lynn Rajskub and Nick Turner titled How to Be a Single Parent, and continues to perform stand-up across the country. events.description: Declared by Jazziz Magazine as “one of the most exciting artists to emerge this past decade,” Vincent Ingala remains an unstoppable and ever-adventurous creative force in urban contemporary jazz, with a total of ten #1 Billboard hits, twenty-three Top 10 singles, and more to come from his latest release and 8th studio album, Escape With Me on Shanachie Entertainment. Upon exploding onto the scene in 2010 with his independent, critically acclaimed debut album North End Soul at the age of 17, Vincent was already a seasoned performer, developing somewhat of a cult following in his home state of Connecticut during his high school years with his compelling one man show. That fan base grew exponentially across the U.S. – and in Europe, thanks to supportive on-line outlets – with his breakthrough single and Top 15 Billboard track “It Is What It Is.” Eleven years after the first time he earned Billboard’s designation as Smooth Jazz Artist of the Year, the saxophonist, multi-instrumentalist, composer, producer and long-beloved entertainer achieved this accolade again in 2023 upon the success of his hit singles “Ridin’ the Wave” and “Shadow Dancer,” the latter of which stayed at #1 on the Smooth Jazz Airplay chart for three weeks. Vincent’s unique dual ability to electrify fans while connecting emotionally with them has made him one of the genre’s most popular touring artists. He draws the audience in and makes them part of an exciting musical experience that bridges the gap between the music of his father’s R&B, funk and soul collection (which Vincent grew up heavily immersed in) and Vincent’s own crisp grooves, well executed horn lines and horn-drenched melodies. Just as he plays every instrument on his self-produced albums, he fronts his explosive band by providing the audience with a well blended show of sax, guitar, drums and vocals. events.description: Email Lee at Lsmith@clpvd.org to be added to the email list about upcoming tufting workshops. You will receive a registration link via email when new workshops are scheduled. Learn how to use a tufting machine and create your own rug in this workshop for adults! In this intensive 4-hour workshop for adults, you will learn the basics of using a tufting machine and complete a small rug. The workshop is free, but participants are required to bring their own yarn (two skeins of yarn per color). Yarn should be a medium weight (4) and feed from the center. All participants are required to satisfactorily complete a safety screening checklist and sign a liability waiver before participating. This intensive 4-hour workshop involves using a handheld power tool with sharp, fast-moving scissors and a needle. If you have, or are recovering from, a hand, wrist, arm, shoulder, or joint injury or condition, you should not participate in this program at this time. Additionally, please ask yourself the following safety screening questions before deciding to participate. If the answer to any of these questions is “no,” you should not participate in this program at this time. Can you stand unassisted while holding a 5-pound power tool with both hands for 3 hours? Can you fully understand and follow directions? (This workshop is conducted in English.) Are you complete the project independently? Can you hold the trigger firmly on a vibrating power tool for 3 hours? Do you have the upper body strength to apply pressure with a handheld power tool and maintain your balance in the event of kickback? Can you carefully handle a handheld power tool with a fast-moving needle? Registration through Eventbrite is required. Please register for only one workshop. If you’ve already completed a workshop and wish to continue tufting, you may do so during makerspace open studio hours.

events.summary: Actor/Comedian/Writer Nick Thune’s deadpan delivery and absurdist storytelling has made him a standout in the comedy world.
events.description: Actor/Comedian/Writer Nick Thune’s deadpan delivery and absurdist storytelling has made him a standout in the comedy world. Originally from Seattle, Thune built his name on late-night stages, racking up ten appearances on The Tonight Show, along with spots on Conan and Late Night. He went on to tour internationally and headline major comedy festivals including Montreal’s Just for Laughs, SXSW, Bonnaroo, and Melbourne International. Thune has released three stand-up specials: Folk Hero (Netflix) and Good Guy (Amazon), and Born Young, which premiered on Nate Bargatze’s Nateland YouTube channel. His material blends sharp one-liners with personal storytelling with guitar, making him a favorite among longtime comedy fans and new audiences alike. On screen, he’s appeared in Judd Apatow’s Knocked Up, Marvel’s Venom, and cult indie Dave Made a Maze, with TV credits including HBO Max’s Love Life, Hulu’s How I Met Your Father, ABC’s Not Dead Yet, Grand Crew and voice work on American Dad!. In 2025, Nick’s short film “BDAY Private Dick” with John C. Reilly premiered at the Palm Springs Film Festival. Currently, Thune is developing a podcast with Mary Lynn Rajskub and Nick Turner titled How to Be a Single Parent, and continues to perform stand-up across the country. events.title: John Cafferty and The Beaver Brown Band
events.summary: The legendary Rhode Island multi-platinum rock'n'roll group
events.description: The legendary Rhode Island multi-platinum rock'n'roll group JOHN CAFFERTY & THE BEAVER BROWN BAND began their career in 1973 and achieved mainstream success in the 1980s with the "Eddie & The Cruisers - Motion Picture Soundtrack". The hit single “ON THE DARK SIDE" held the “#1” position on the Billboard Rock charts and the MTV video charts for five consecutive weeks. The album sold over 3 million copies and was certified triple Platinum by the RIAA. The title track from the group's 1985 follow-up album “TOUGH ALL OVER” became their second “#1” single on the Billboard Rock charts and the song “C-I-T-Y” reached the Billboard Top 20. John Cafferty's solo track “HEARTS ON FIRE" was featured in Sylvester Stallone’s film "ROCKY IV” and he received his second double Platinum two million selling soundtrack award. Over the years John has placed 35 songs in major motion pictures. Today John Cafferty & The Beaver Brown Band continue to tour and bring their exciting live shows to fans around the world. In 2012 they were inducted into the Rhode Island Music Hall Of Fame. 2022 marked the release of JOHN CAFFERTY & THE BEAVER BROWN BAND'S GREATEST HITS on Iconoclassic Records. A comprehensive collection of all “original recordings” from their hit albums and movie soundtracks. In the Spring of 2025 in celebration of their 50+ years together JOHN CAFFERTY & THE BEAVER BROWN BAND released "SOUND OF WAVES" a long awaited and critcally acclaimed album of brand new songs. The pre-released single “DAY IN THE SUN” has received 5 star reviews and is climbing the national classic rock radio and streaming charts. And following in the band's decades long movie soundtrack legacy it is featured in the 2024 Peter Farrelly film “Ricky Stanicky” starring Zac Efron and John Cena. In 2026 SONY MUSIC released a digital version of JCBBB's GREATEST HITS available on all major streaming platforms.

Live From South High blends stand-up and storytelling to tell the unlikely journey that took Orlando from student, to teacher, to the comedy stage—and what it means to leave one version of your life behind and start another. events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/479711 --- Hallucinatory, evocative, and surreal in its own idiosyncratic way, Hot Fruit is Erinrose Mager’s long awaited debut volume. Strange and incantatory, Erinrose Mager’s debut collection Hot Fruit investigates the longing for self, the longing for another, and the longing for connection between the self and another when the other is inherently unknowable. The pieces in this collection constellate sensations of familial loss and longing, class and financial precarity, culinary ritual, fractured memory, and the peculiarity of placelessness, interspersed with a fable cycle that reimagines Korean myths, legends, and contemporary media through the lens of the adoptee experience.

events.summary: Do you have your own creative project in mind? We have makerspace equipment, tools, and supplies that might be useful! Some smaller hand tools and art supplies that are available include: a button/pin maker, tracing light pad, cutting mat…
events.description: Do you have your own creative project in mind? We have makerspace equipment, tools, and supplies that might be useful! Some smaller hand tools and art supplies that are available include: a button/pin maker, tracing light pad, cutting mat with rotary cutters, iron, clamps, painting supplies, stencil brushes, Perler beads, hot glue, ribbon, yarn, corner rounder punch, and more. Feel free to stop by to use one of these tools during an open studio session! In addition, we offer access to machines including: Silhouette and Cricut cutting machines, sewing machines, a sublimation printer, a 3D printer, an Epilog laser cutter, and heat presses for fabric and mugs. If you are new to using one of these machines, it is best to receive an introductory lesson by appointment first to learn the basics. To begin using one of the machines, please follow these steps: First, we encourage you to request a training to learn the basics of a specific machine beforehand. We can set up a separate appointment to meet with you during the week. After you are trained, continue working on independent projects during open studio sessions! This month, we are hosting studio sessions for adults on Monday evenings 5:00-7:30, Wednesday mornings 10:00-1:00, and Friday afternoons 1:00-5:00 at Rochambeau Library. If you are planning to attend a particular studio session, it is helpful to RSVP with Garrett at glocke@clpvd.org so we can predict which machines will be in demand.

events.title: A View From The Bridge
events.summary: "Just remember, kid, you can quicker get back a million dollars that was stolen than a word that you gave away." On the Brooklyn waterfront, longshoreman Eddie Carbone lives by a strict code of loyalty, family, and respect.
events.description: "Just remember, kid, you can quicker get back a million dollars that was stolen than a word that you gave away." On the Brooklyn waterfront, longshoreman Eddie Carbone lives by a strict code of loyalty, family, and respect. But when two undocumented cousins arrive from Sicily seeking work, Eddie’s tightly controlled world begins to unravel. His growing obsession with his niece Catherine sets off a chain reaction of suspicion, betrayal, and devastating consequences. In one of the most powerful tragedies of the American stage, Miller lays bare the destructive force of jealousy and pride.

events.title: K Chiucarello reading from NANNY NANNY, along with Courtney Denelle
events.summary: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/479712 --- “Nanny Nanny is absolutely stunning. Exquisitely crafted, with visceral intensity throughout.
events.description: Latest event details: https://riffraffevents.eventcalendarapp.com/u/39909/479712 --- “Nanny Nanny is absolutely stunning. Exquisitely crafted, with visceral intensity throughout. I loved it.”—Elliot Page “In the midst of so many literary reconsiderations of motherhood, this book announces itself as an essential left-field addition to the contemporary canon . . . Nanny Nanny comes at you like an incendiary secret, a sweet and dangerous flame kindled in the dark.”—Jia Tolentino, New York Times bestselling author of Trick Mirror A single, 35-year-old career nanny decides to have a baby of her own in this incandescent debut novel unsettling traditional narratives about motherhood, gender, class, domestic violence, and the politics and labor of care. After years of caring full-time for the children of the rich and the famous, our narrator has been struck, finally, with baby fever. Over a drink with sympathetic friends, she lists all the reasons why she wants to have a baby, beginning with a story about the intoxicating, abusive relationship with an ex-wife that she barely survived. She ponders how to fill the gaping void left in the wake of such horrific domestic violence. What’s the next most violent thing a woman can do to herself? she asks. Have a baby. Soon, her story opens other doors to the past—the seemingly idyllic childhood she spent under her father’s roof; the mentorship, and judgment, of female writers whose children she has reared; and the man, her first love, who now seems to be offering her a second chance. Each unraveling thread reveals the complex tangle of thrill and pain, tradition and progress that has led her to this moment, this calling. Is it time for her to become a mother? K Chiucarello’s stunningly original debut novel explores the brutality of gendered violence, including the gossip that polices women’s choices and the conventions that determine which women have the right to tell their story, and how. events.summary: Jessimae Peluso is a stand-up comedian, writer, and podcast host whose comedy blends raw honesty with sharp, high-energy punchlines.
events.description: Jessimae Peluso is a stand-up comedian, writer, and podcast host whose comedy blends raw honesty with sharp, high-energy punchlines. Best known for her breakout role on MTV's Girl Code, she's also hosted Netflix's Tattoo Redo and Surviving Paradise. With nearly two decades in comedy, Jessimae has built a reputation for turning personal chaos into catharsis—especially after losing both of her parents. That experience fuels her advocacy work with Hilarity for Charity and the Alzheimer's Association, where she uses humor to bring visibility and humanity to conversations around grief and brain health. Jessimae has performed worldwide with the USO, entertaining troops in Japan, Iraq, Poland, Norway, Bahrain, and Afghanistan. Her stand-up has been featured at Just For Laughs, New York Comedy Festival, and MoonTower, with TV appearances including The Joe Rogan Experience, Chelsea Lately, @Midnight, and Lights Out with David Spade. Her podcast, Dying Laughing with Jessimae, launched in 2025 with longtime friend John Stamos as the first guest and explores grief, loss, and survival—with just enough inappropriate jokes to make it all bearable. On stage, Jessimae delivers fearless, deeply relatable comedy that makes audiences laugh hard, feel seen, and leave lighter than they arrived. Tickets: https://www.ricomedyconnection.com/events/jessimae-peluso-2026

events.summary: Free Open Houses at the Betsey Williams Cottage in Roger Williams Park on Fridays, 10am-3pm! Step back in time to explore the Betsey Williams Cottage, built in 1773 and home to Roger Williams’ great-great-great granddaughters, Betsey and…
events.description: Free Open Houses at the Betsey Williams Cottage in Roger Williams Park on Fridays, 10am-3pm! Step back in time to explore the Betsey Williams Cottage, built in 1773 and home to Roger Williams’ great-great-great granddaughters, Betsey and Rhoda Williams. Upon her death in 1871, Betsey Williams bequeathed the cottage and 102 acres of surrounding farmland to the city of Providence, which became the foundation of Roger Williams Park. Drop-in during these FREE open houses to learn about the Cottage’s history and its significance to Roger Williams Park. The open houses are FREE and open to the public. Presented by the Museum of Natural History and Planetarium . The Betsey Williams Cottage is located near Roger Williams Park’s Elmwood Avenue entrance. Parking is available on streets surrounding the Rose Garden; see a Roger Williams Park map .

While also a master of the roast, the legendary Roast of Rich Vos is considered one of the best and most successful of all time. Rich has performed everywhere from corporate events, golf outings and 12-step conventions to hosting Woodstock '99, the Opie &Anthony Virus Tour, and the annual benefit honoring his late friend and comedy icon Patrice O'Neal. Rich is a proud husband, father of three and grandfather with 39 years of sobriety. His raw honesty, quick wit, and relentless drive make him a true original in the world of comedy. events.title: November Open House: The Museum at the John Brown House
events.venue: The Museum at the John Brown House
events.summary: On Saturday, November 28, 2026, start the holiday season by stepping back into the 17th century at the Museum at the John Brown House for our November Open House.
events.description: On Saturday, November 28, 2026, start the holiday season by stepping back into the 17th century at the Museum at the John Brown House for our November Open House. Inspired by the Mary Williams exhibit, this family-friendly event offers a captivating look at Rhode Island’s early history. What happens when an idealist gets the chance to put his ideas into practice, and then lives long enough to see the consequences? At 11am, experience Two Rogers: Hope and Consequence, a unique living history presentation featuring Daniel Perkins and John McNiff portraying founder Roger Williams at two pivotal moments in his life as they examine the complex legacy of his early ideals. In 1645, a younger Williams looks upon Rhode Island as “A Place to Begin,” giving thanks for the land, people, and opportunity to build something new. Twenty years later, an older Williams asks “What Has Endured?” Looking back on friendships and conflicts, successes and disappointments, he considers what became of those early hopes. Through land, people, and ideals, Two Rogers explores Thanksgiving not as a holiday, but as a question: after nearly 30 years of the Rhode Island experiment, for what should Roger Williams give thanks? Throughout the day, visitors can enjoy ongoing historical clothing discussions with living historian Kristel Henry, who will explore the layers and stories behind 17th-century women’s garments. Younger visitors can join in historical crafts, and the museum galleries will be open for exploring. Admission to the open house is pay-as-you-wish, and donations are warmly welcomed. While exploring early Rhode Island history and enjoying a sweet treat, jump-start your holiday shopping in the museum shop, which features one-of-a-kind, exclusive RIHS merchandise. Located at 52 Power Street in Providence, The Museum at the John Brown House is open from 10am-4pm. Registration is requested, but not required; seating for the 11am talk is limited. events.title: PVD Banned Book Club
events.summary: In 2023 over 4,000 unique titles have been either banned or challenged across the country. These book bans tend to target subjects concerning Race and LGBTQ+ topics.
events.description: In 2023 over 4,000 unique titles have been either banned or challenged across the country. These book bans tend to target subjects concerning Race and LGBTQ+ topics. However, those challenging the books are stating they’re harmful to children, offensive, vulgar and even pornographic. PVD Banned Books Club wants to know what’s really going on- are these books dangerous? Or is there more happening behind the curtain? Together we hope to have open, honest, and respectful conversations about the book ban phenomenon and explore what happens when we allow censorship to take storm. This is an open forum about book topics, characters, and issues that are being deemed controversial. Some reads are easy, and some topics can be heavy, but we consider them all necessary. For this month’s selection, email rocadults@clpvd.org and/or mar.lee.1987@gmail.com

events.title: Rich Vos
events.summary: Rich Vos is a comedy powerhouse with over 100 television appearances and a career that spans decades. He's a recurring guest on Gutfeld!, can be heard on The Joe Rogan Experience, SiriusXM, as well as countless podcasts.
events.description: Rich Vos is a comedy powerhouse with over 100 television appearances and a career that spans decades. He's a recurring guest on Gutfeld!, can be heard on The Joe Rogan Experience, SiriusXM, as well as countless podcasts. Rich has cemented his place as one of the most respected voices in stand-up comedy, with several groundbreaking television appearances including the inaugural seasons of Last Comic Standing, the first white performer on Def Jam Comedy and as a regular on Tough Crowd with Colin Quinn. Rich Vos has been showcased on platforms including Netflix, Amazon Prime, Showtime and more. Beyond stand-up Rich has been featured in films such as The King of Staten Island, Women Aren't Funny, and the acclaimed Patrice O'Neal: Killing Is Easy documentary. While also a master of the roast, the legendary Roast of Rich Vos is considered one of the best and most successful of all time. Rich has written for two Academy Awards broadcasts, released four Comedy Central specials, an Amazon Prime special, and the multi-platform 30 Minutes with Rich Vos, along with seven comedy albums showcasing the sharp wit and authenticity that have become his signature. Rich has performed everywhere from corporate events, golf outings and 12-step conventions to hosting Woodstock '99, the Opie &Anthony Virus Tour, and the annual benefit honoring his late friend and comedy icon Patrice O'Neal. Rich is a proud husband, father of three and grandfather with 39 years of sobriety. His raw honesty, quick wit, and relentless drive make him a true original in the world of comedy. Some smaller hand tools and art supplies that are available include: a button/pin maker, tracing light pad, cutting mat with rotary cutters, iron, clamps, painting supplies, stencil brushes, Perler beads, hot glue, ribbon, yarn, corner rounder punch, and more. events.title: British Soldiers’ Wives in the American Revolution: A Talk with Author Don Hagist
events.venue: The Museum at the John Brown House
events.summary: On Thursday, December 3, 2026, at 5:30pm, the Museum at the John Brown House will host author Don N. Hagist for British Soldiers’ Wives in the American Revolution, a talk based on his new book, Invisible Lives.
events.description: On Thursday, December 3, 2026, at 5:30pm, the Museum at the John Brown House will host author Don N. Hagist for British Soldiers’ Wives in the American Revolution, a talk based on his new book, Invisible Lives. During the Revolutionary War, thousands of women followed their soldier husbands across the Atlantic, enduring the hardships of garrisons, sieges, and camp life in a foreign land. Though these women nursed the wounded, raised children, and performed vital labor in every theater of the conflict, their individual stories have been largely lost to history. Combining meticulous archival research with deeply human storytelling, Hagist draws on court-martial proceedings, muster rolls, newspaper notices, and rare surviving letters to reconstruct their lived experiences—revealing a portrait of remarkable resourcefulness and resilience. Don N. Hagist is the managing editor of the Journal of the American Revolution and an expert on the British Army during the American Revolution. He is the author of several acclaimed books, including Noble Volunteers: The British Soldiers Who Fought the American Revolution and The Revolution’s Last Men. Doors open at 4:30 pm for a reception and book signing. General admission costs $10 per person, $5 for RIHS members; a combo book-admission ticket is also available. Registration is requested as seating is limited. Guests can register here .

events.title: Janeane Garofalo
events.summary: Actress and comedian Janeane Garofalo has been an American institution since she burst on the scene in 1992. Janeane has had many memorable and critically acclaimed roles in films such as "The Truth About Cats and Dogs," “Wet Hot American…
events.description: Actress and comedian Janeane Garofalo has been an American institution since she burst on the scene in 1992. Janeane has had many memorable and critically acclaimed roles in films such as "The Truth About Cats and Dogs," “Wet Hot American Summer,” “Ratatouille,” "Steal This Movie," "Reality Bites," "Romy and Michelle's High School Reunion," "Mystery Men," “The Ten” and "The Cable Guy". Janeane also co-authored the best seller "Feel This Book," with Ben Stiller. Janeane was a cast member of the Emmy Award-winning Ben Stiller Show and played the role of Paula, the acerbic talent booker, on "The Larry Sanders Show," for which she received an Emmy nomination. During the fall of '94 she joined the cast of "Saturday Night Live." Some of Janeane's other television work includes two specials for HBO, FOX’s “24,” “Mad About You," and the final season of NBC's "The West Wing," where she played Democratic campaign strategist Louise Thornton. In addition to acting in film and television, Janeane is an outspoken activist, spoken word performer and stand-up comedy entertainer known and respected around the world. She was instrumental in the successful launching of the first liberal radio network, Air America Radio, where she hosted her own talk show, "The Majority Report." A lightning rod for controversy, Janeane's well informed opinions and unflinching honesty have inspired laughs, as well as striking a chord with the left, right and everyone in between.
